findings.text: Top-level nested controls setup initializes the nested MSR area from hardware configuration and EPT capabilities by delegating pin, exit, entry, primary, secondary, misc, basic and fixed-control groups to dedicated helpers, then publishing a VMCS enumeration value.

VMCS12 field offset lookup validates that the encoding fits addressable range and mapped table bounds, applies speculative index hardening, and reports missing entries with a not-found status, otherwise returning the stored table offset.

VMCS12 table position and hardware encoding are related by a 16-bit rotation, while the architecture field index is obtained by masking and shifting the encoding; enumeration value is the largest index present in the sparse table shifted into position.

Nested pin controls expose only a small allow-list derived from host execution configuration plus mandatory always-on bits and timer support, with posted-interrupt exposure conditional on a global toggle.

Exit and entry control advertisements intersect host controls with a narrow set of state load and save features, always add mandatory plus extended-feature and performance-control handling, drop CET handling when neither CET feature is present, and permit free guest control of debug-control save and load by clearing the corresponding must-be-one bits.

Primary processor controls advertise a bounded set of exiting, windowing, bitmap and shadowing behaviours from host configuration, always add mandatory bits and MSR-bitmap use even when host lacks it, and allow free guest control of CR3 access interceptions.

Secondary controls advertise descriptor, timestamp, APIC virtualization, exit-on-instruction and extended feature subsets from host configuration, always emulate VMCS shadowing, and conditionally add EPT with capability masking, VPID, unrestricted guest, APIC access virtualization, page-modification logging, mode-based execution, EPTP-switching VMFUNC and enclave exiting according to global toggles and hardware support.

Miscellaneous nested data preserves only the host save-EFER indicator plus read-only shadow, timer-rate and activity hints, basic info encodes emulated VMCS revision size and type with true-controls and optional host passthrough flags, and fixed CR ranges enforce VMXON always-on bits while fixed-one bits are read from hardware with optional emulated masking addition.
VMXON requires protection, paging and numeric-error bits fixed on in CR0 and virtual-machine extensions fixed on in CR4, representing the mandatory guest fixed-zero values for nested operation.

VMCS12 field table initialization iterates the supported-offset list and installs an entry only when a nonzero offset is supplied and the running CPU provides that field, advancing the population count past the last installed position.

Per-field hardware gating maps identifiers such as VPID, posted-interrupt, TSC scaling, TPR shadow, APIC access, interrupt delivery, VM function, EPT, XSAVES, enclave bitmap, performance control, secondary execution and CET state to corresponding CPU capability queries, while preemption timer, page-log index and all unlisted fields are unconditionally accepted as emulated.
Paired 64-bit VMCS fields are handled by treating high and low halves as one case, so capability gating applies jointly to both halves.

SGX launch-enclave hash setup uses built-in default hash words when SGX is disabled, launch control is available, or the first hash MSR cannot be read; otherwise it snapshots the four current hardware hash MSRs.
An alternate SGX hash setup variant provides an empty operation that performs no initialization, indicating a build without SGX support.
Maximum EPT page-walk depth is five levels only when five-level EPT is supported, otherwise four levels.

CPU capability initialization starts from generic state, then conditionally advertises virtualization, protection, tracing, debugging, performance, SGX family, user-interrupt masking, XSAVES, timestamp and wait-package features according to nested mode, hardware queries and global enables, and disables CET features unless CET, unrestricted guest and no-hardware-error-code behaviour are all present.

Guest performance capabilities are zero when the PMU is disabled, otherwise begin with firmware-write support and add host branch-record format only with call-stack support outside mediated modes, plus host precise-event mask while explicitly excluding adaptive precise-event behaviour.

Preemption timer setup disables the feature when hardware lacks it, scales host timestamp frequency by the VMCS rate factor, computes an architectural maximum from hypervisor presence and timestamp calibration leaves, and disables the timer when even its maximum value would fire too frequently, otherwise leaving hypervisor timer hooks installed.
An alternate preemption-timer setup is a no-op, representing builds without timer support.

User-return MSR setup registers a fixed small list covering syscall-related, extended-feature, auxiliary timestamp, star and transactional-control MSRs, asserting at build time that the list length matches the reserved capacity.

Memory-encryption SPTE masking treats the gap between boot physical bits and host maximum physical address as KeyID reservation on multi-key capable systems, and installs zero encryption bits with that reservation as the reserved mask.

Hardware teardown clears posted-interrupt wakeup handling and conditionally releases nested shadow resources only when nesting is enabled, with a top dispatcher also releasing trusted-domain capacity when trusted domains are enabled.
Trusted-domain hardware teardown releases its miscellaneous cgroup capacity by resetting its limit to zero.
Virtual-machine initialization dispatches to trusted-domain initialization for trusted guests and to standard VMX initialization otherwise.
VMCS12 offset lookup hardens the table index against speculation and treats zero offsets as absent, which matters because the table is documented as very sparsely populated.

Preemption timer is abandoned when calibration implies spurious exits could occur faster than a low-frequency threshold, preventing excessive exits from using the maximum timer value as a disable mechanism.
Adaptive precise-event capability is deliberately masked out to avoid functional defects, potential host state disclosure via branch records, and bypass of userspace event filtering.

Observed nested MSR container holds low and high pairs for pin, exit, entry, primary and secondary controls plus misc low and high, basic, fixed-zero and fixed-one CR values, EPT and VPID capability words, VMFUNC controls and a VMCS enumeration word.
